text: In World War Two, Britain seriously planned an aircraft carrier made of ice. The secret was pykrete: ice mixed with about fourteen percent wood pulp. The fibres stop cracks spreading, so it is much tougher than ice, and melts slower. Project Habakkuk would have been six hundred metres long, kept frozen by refrigeration pipes. A small prototype was built on a lake in Canada. In one famous demonstration, a bullet shattered a block of ice, then bounced right off the pykrete. Costs kept climbing, and the ice ship was cancelled. Dave was standing where the bullet bounced.
